## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

Commit only when the user 322 says so; **commit messages carry NO AI attribution.** 323 2. ~~**Commit the grants-fix migration**~~ **DONE** — `20260721090000_authenticated_grants.sql` is committed 324 (in `fa8176b`, alongside `20260721100000_profile_location.sql`). 325 3. ~~**Weather → real location.**~~ **DONE 2026-07-21** (8 commits on `feat/stylist-generator`, live-verified). 326 Geolocation fires **on tap** of "Use my location" in the city menu (never on load — a sticky `Block` is 327 the thing to avoid); the fix persists to `profiles.location_lat/lon/label/source/timezone/updated_at` and 328 silently refreshes on later loads when the browser already reports `granted`. **A saved city beats GPS** 329 (`location_source = 'city'` suppresses the refresh); an explicit tap still wins. **Open-Meteo needs no key.** 330 Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-21-generator-real-location-design.md` · plan: 331 `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-21-generator-real-location.md`. 332 Three defects were fixed alongside it: 333 - **Hour labels were GMT.** No `timezone` param was sent, so the "Later" cells showed UTC — 2h off in 334 Berlin. file.content: # Session Handoff / Project State Command:resume _Last updated: 2026-07-30 (PRs #14–#19 merged; nothing in flight; queue #4 is next). Read this first when resuming._ > **What this file is authoritative for:** rejected approaches, superseded plans, > open-but-uninvestigated issues, and loose ends — the things `git` structurally cannot tell you. > **Branches, commits, and what's merged come from `git`, never from here.** > > **The one staleness check:** if the in-flight branch named below ≠ `git branch --show-current`, > this narrative is behind — say so, and trust git for the facts. An ordinary implementation commit > does *not* make it stale. Whoever changes branch state updates this section **at that moment**, > not at session end. --- ## TL;DR — where we are (2026-07-28) **The full magic-moment loop is on `main` and merged.** Sign in → onboarding → capture → closet → generate outfits. The generator, real location/weather, the occasion-model fix, and the Refine colour lean all landed via PRs #5–#8. **Merged (PRs #9–#12):** the **daily-drop model** (looks generated once per local day per occasion, persisted to `outfits`, occasion tap reads the stored set — Decision 5 in CLAUDE.md); **WebP cutouts** (~75% smaller); **signed-URL cache** (stable URLs so the browser reuses images). Also on main: a **CI workflow** (`verify`: test + tsc + build) and a **`main` branch ruleset** (require PR + `verify` green, block force-push/deletion). A `main` is now protected — always branch → PR → green → merge. **Merged (PR #13): smart default occasion.** Replaced the once-considered "What's today?" morning question (rejected — a daily gate in front of the magic moment). The app *predicts* the occasion each morning (rule + onboarding `occasions`: weekday→Work if they dress for it else Everyday, weekend→Weekend), shows a legible "why" label, and **logs every override** to `occasion_overrides` — banked for the future learner (below). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-smart-default-occasion-design.md`. `main` HEAD is `1886409`. **Merged (PR #14): generator coverage** — branch `fix/generator-coverage`, now on `main`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/todo/2026-07-24-generator-audit.md`. Measurement-first: a coverage probe went in *before* any fix. Four defects fixed — top-major nested-loop truncation (now breadth-first, so the candidate cap samples the whole closet), index-0 pinning for outerwear/ accessories, a missing distinctness check in re-ranking, and out-of-range index handling. Measured reachability on a 20-item closet: tops **1→20**, bottoms **5→20**, shoes 20→20, coats **1→3**, accessories **1→3**. A diversity pre-filter now sits between ranking and the AI re-ranker so the day's three looks cannot share a top or bottom, and the shortlist is **never padded with repeats** to reach the requested count. **✅ RESOLVED — Regenerate. Merged (PR #15), `main` HEAD `d7ce07a`. Nothing in flight.** Symptom confirmed with the user: the same looks came back. Two causes, and the second was bigger than the audit plan's suspect list anticipated. 1. **The shortlist collapsed.** `diversify` kept a combo only when its top *and* bottom were both unused, then backfilled to a floor of 3 — so at most `min(distinct tops, distinct bottoms)` survived. Measured on the real 21-item closet: **48 valid combos → 6 handed to the model in summer, 21 → 3 in winter.** In winter the model picked 3 from 3, so Regenerate *could not* differ. All shoe variation lived in the discarded combos. Now tiered (fresh top+bottom → one fresh slot → the rest), filled to `n`: **20 in every season.** This reverses part of `2e88d39` — right that padding with duplicates is bad, wrong that a combo sharing one slot is a duplicate. 2. **S1 was correct but incomplete** — the pipeline is deterministic and `excludeItemIds` was `[]`. **Fixed with a SOFT preference, not `excludeItemIds`.** `Ctx.recentlyShown` applies a proportional score penalty (`RECENT_WEIGHT = 0.25` in `rank.ts`) so just-shown pieces sink but are never removed. **A hard filter was measured and rejected:** excluding the previous set's tops+bottoms yields **0 combos in winter** on this closet — the same hard-filter trap already fixed for outerwear and the shoes formality floor. `excludeItemIds` stays unused, reserved for a genuinely hard exclusion (cleaners, packing). **S2 and S3 were ruled out by inspection** — the client passes `regenerate: true` via a direct call, and `saveDailyLooks` failures surface as a caught error state. **A pre-existing bug was found while verifying** and fixed on the same branch: `RerankSchema` demanded *exactly* 3 picks, but `forStructuredOutput` strips `minItems`/`maxItems`, so the count was never enforced on the model — it was only a post-hoc throw. **Any closet with fewer than three viable combos failed the whole generation as "Couldn't reach the stylist", including one straight out of onboarding's "capture your first five"** — i.e. at the magic moment. Now `.min(1)` with the cap in `finalisePicks`. Live-verified: a 3-item closet renders its one look and Regenerate returns it again with a fresh "why". **Plan review (2026-07-27) — read before executing anything from `todo/`.** `docs/superpowers/plans/REVIEW-2026-07-27.md`. Every plan was read against the current code. **Nine factual defects were fixed in the plan files themselves** (the plans on disk are already corrected) — including one that mattered: `seasons-soft-preference`, which is **#1 in the execution order**, pasted a pre-fix `buildCandidates` and would have silently reverted the coverage work on this branch. Because `docs/` is gitignored there is no diff for those edits, so the review file is the only record of what changed and why. It also lists what was deliberately *not* changed (product decisions, not defects), one substitution in `wear-stats` that needs a second opinion, and the items checked and found fine — so none of it is re-litigated next session. **Merged (PR #17): the composition guard.** `lib/generator/__tests__/pipeline-integration.test.ts` — tests only. PRs #14/#15/#16 each had unit tests and none checked them *together*, though all three rewrote the same pipeline. It walks `buildCandidates → rankTopN → diversify` across all 16 occasion × season combinations and asserts each PR's guarantee still holds in the presence of the other two. **If you touch the generator, this is the file that tells you what you broke.** **Merged (PR #18): design tokens** — plan in `done/2026-07-24-design-tokens.md`. Added the missing cream step (`--color-value` `#cfc8ba`, the right-hand side of every label/value pair), a 7-weight `--hairline-*` elevation scale, and three surface gradients (`.surface-card`, `.surface-stage`, `.surface-strip`). Applied to the item card, the nav and the capture FAB. Three deliberate divergences from that plan, all because the design file said otherwise: the card gradient went into the **`Surface` primitive** (one consumer; later screens inherit it); the card's image div takes **no fill** (the design has none, and ours was covering the gradient); idle nav tabs are `--muted-dim`, not `--muted-foreground`. **The bottom nav is now a floating pill and its active tab is cream, not rust** — the design defines `tabActive='#EDE6D8'`, and rust there spent a second rust on every screen against the One Rust Rule. **⚠️ Tailwind v4 gotcha, learned the hard way:** utilities sit AFTER components in the layer order, so a `bg-*` utility beside `.surface-card` wins and silently restores the flat fill. `Surface`'s test guards this. Also: the theme token is `--color-brand`, there is no `--brand` — an undefined var renders nothing. **Merged (PR #19): item data completeness** — plan in `done/2026-07-24-item-data-completeness.md`. `lib/closet/vocab.ts` is now the single source for every closet vocabulary; `CATEGORIES`/`SEASONS` are derived from `TagSchema` so drift is impossible, and a test asserts neither edit screen re-declares them. `material` and `texture` are now `z.enum` — the model is constrained, not asked nicely. New `items.texture` column (knit structure, which `material` cannot express). `colors`, `pattern`, `subcategory` and `price` became editable on both surfaces — `colors` matters most because it feeds `colorHarmonyScore`, so a mis-read colour silently degraded every outfit ranked. **Next plan is queue #4, `outfit-detail-wear-logging`** — the README calls it "the unblocker": the "Wear this today" button is the only wear-log write path in the product, and six surfaces read what it writes. Queues #1, #2 and #3 are done. **Plans still queued** in `docs/superpowers/plans/todo/`: regenerate-quota → cutout-backfill → route-url-audit (runs last; reworks `/generate` → `/today`, occasion-in-URL, `/outfits/[id]`, manifest, revalidation). Note: `intent-first-entry` is superseded by the smart-default feature above. The 2026-07-24 batch (design-tokens, entitlements, fit-diary, item-detail-rebuild, wear-stats, settings, profile-hub, …) is planned but unstarted. **Future (deferred, data being captured now): the occasion learner.** Personalizes the morning default from the logged `occasion_overrides`. Build it once real override data has accumulated — not sooner (it can't behave differently from the rule until history exists, and its learning rule is best designed against real patterns). Slots into `predictOccasion` via an optional `history` arg — additive, no rewrite. Rejected alternative: real-calendar integration (trust/GDPR cost > value). Full design in the spec above; see the `future-occasion-learner` auto-memory. **⚠️ The local closet was MODIFIED by the backfill (2026-07-29).** `scripts/backfill-item-tags.ts` normalised 15 of 29 rows onto the constrained vocabulary — `"cotton"` → `Cotton`, `"Cotton knit"` → `Cotton`, `"Polyester, Viscose"` → `Polyester`, `"knit"` → `Other`, `"leather"` → `Leather`. The closet now holds 8 distinct materials, all valid. **`texture` is still null on all 29 rows**: filling it re-tags each item via Haiku (~6¢ for this closet) and is deliberately manual, because running it accidentally on every dev machine is worse than leaving it null — every consumer already treats null as "no opinion". Re-running the script is safe and idempotent. **Two migrations landed with #19**, and the second was unplanned: `20260724090000_item_texture.sql`, and `20260729090000_service_role_grants.sql`. The backfill hit `42501 permission denied` because **`service_role` bypasses RLS but NOT table privileges** — the same gap `20260721090000` closed for `authenticated`. Nothing in the app runs as `service_role`; the grant creates no bypass. `supabase db diff` is clean. **⚠️ `HOT_MATERIALS` deliberately survived #19** — see the staged plan above. Queue #3 gave it the `items.texture` column it needs, but the replacement happens at **queue #12**, not before. A test in `lib/closet/__tests__/vocab.test.ts` now asserts every material it names still exists in the vocabulary, so it cannot silently stop matching now that `material` is an enum. **Layout trap worth remembering** (cost two attempts on #19): an `` that is a **grid item** keeps `min-height: auto`, so its intrinsic size can force the row past an `aspect-[…]` ratio — and `max-h-full` does NOT save it, because a percentage against an auto-sized grid row is indefinite and resolves to `none`. Safari spilled a 970×1280 cutout right over the fields below. The fix is `absolute inset-0 size-full object-contain` inside a `relative` box, which gives `object-contain` a definite box. Chrome tolerated it; the simulator did not — another reason to judge on device. **Long vocabularies are SELECTS, not chips** (user decision, 2026-07-29). 27 materials and 16 textures as chip rows filled most of a phone screen. `components/ui-fitcheck/select.tsx` is the primitive; on iOS it opens the native wheel. Chips stay for short sets — category (5), seasons (4). The colour palette collapses to a one-line summary once a colour is chosen and auto-opens when none is. **Not verified live:** the **capture confirm screen**. It carries all the new controls from #19 and its tests pass, but exercising it end-to-end needs a real photo upload. Worth doing when capture is next touched. **Loose ends (not in any plan):** iCloud may still be generating `" 2."` duplicate files (gitignored, but they break `npm run build` via tsc); the impeccable hook flags pre-existing off-ramp font sizes in `refine-sheet.tsx` / `stylist-view.tsx` / `item-card.tsx` — needs its own `/impeccable audit`. _Everything below this line predates 2026-07-22 and describes how the generator first landed — kept for history, but the TL;DR above is current._ --- ## What's on `main` (all merged) | Plan | What | |---|---| | 01 setup · 02 auth · 03 primitives · 04 capture · 05 closet | the base app (auth, onboarding quiz, capture→confirm, closet grid + item edit) | | 04 Task 9 | **onboarding "capture your first five"** — `useCapture` engine extraction + `/onboarding/capture` (merged via PR #4) | `main` HEAD ≈ `40143e1` + a couple of merges since. **CLAUDE.md was removed from git** this session (user deleted it deliberately; now gitignored — see decisions). ## The generator — branch `feat/stylist-generator` (7 commits, DONE, unmerged) Built this session, TDD, **95 tests green · tsc clean · build clean**. Live-verified end-to-end on 2026-07-19: real Open-Meteo weather → deterministic candidates/score/rank → **Haiku re-rank (3 named looks + one-sentence "why")** → flat-lay layout → signed cutout URLs → the screen. The magic moment works. Commits (oldest→newest): - `68c0d50` shared types, `Fragrance` category, outfits/wear schema + RLS - `6e245f4` deterministic engine — occasion bands, colour, score, candidates, rank - `47c942f` deterministic flat-lay **layout templates** (the de-risk: no-clip / ±6° / anchor-first) - `f0486ad` weather — hourly + feels-like + time-aware "Later" advice + city geocoding - `3ad7b74` text-only Haiku re-rank — describe + name/why schema - `34e076c` generate action wires the pipeline → 3 laid-out looks - `c8c3dc7` the v2 screen — weather/city, occasion/refine, flat-lay+motion, why/credits, index, states **Files:** `lib/generator/*` (types, rules, color, score, candidates, rank, layout, rerank), `lib/weather/*` (open-meteo, advice, geocode), `app/generate/actions.ts` (the `generate` action), `components/generate/*` (weather-strip, occasion-row, refine-sheet, flat-lay, why-quote, credits, index-tabs, stylist-view, stylist), `app/generate/page.tsx` (replaced the placeholder). Plan + design decisions in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-18-stylist-generator.md`. ### The design source (authoritative) `design_handoff_stylist_generator/` = a Claude Design handoff. **`README.md` + `generator-mockup-v2.html` are the authoritative spec** (v2 = editorial "Lookbook" with the "Today's Looks" header + weather pill + city + "Later" advice + occasion chips + Refine sheet + 01/02/03 + why-as-hero + credits). `Fitcheck.dc.html` and `generator-mockup-original.html` in that folder are **byte-identical duplicates** — ignore them. ### Review punch-list — all fixed + test-enforced An adversarial review found real issues; every one is baked in as a tested decision (D1–D12 in the plan): - **D1 reduced-motion**: flat-lay is `opacity:1` by default (a plain-`` path when reduced) — motion is progressive enhancement. A test fails if any piece is `opacity:0` under reduce. (Fixes an invisibility bug.) - **D2 contrast**: informational text ≥ `muted-foreground`; credits' **brand names are the most readable**. - **D3** one look name (index === byline). **D4** occasion uses `Chip variant="select"`. **D5** the why leads with the rust "f" glyph. **D6** deterministic layout templates. **D9** occasion→band model. **D10** loading/ empty/error states. **D11** fragrances excluded. **D12** optional accessory slots. --- ## 🎯 The occasion model (reworked 2026-07-21, after PR #5) **Occasion is CONTEXT, not a dress code.** An evening date and a black-tie dinner are both "Evening"; what separates them is the user's dress code. The original narrow bands (work `[3,4.5]`, evening `[3.5,5]`) baked one assumed dress code in for everyone, so a smart-casual wardrobe could not produce a Work or Evening outfit **at all** — the screen just said "Add a few more pieces" with 8 items in the closet. The resolution order is now: **occasion band → narrowed by the profile's dress codes → overridden by Refine.** - Bands widened (`lib/generator/rules.ts`); every band includes 3 (smart casual). - `personalBand()` intersects with `profiles.formality_min/max` — the answer onboarding **already collected** and the generator had never selected. Padded ±0.5; falls back to the plain occasion band when there's no overlap. - `applyFormalityOverride` now REPLACES rather than intersects, so Refine can dress you *up* past your usual ceiling (previously a smart-casual profile could never request black tie). **Related principle — hard filters vs soft preferences.** Three filters could each silently yield zero outfits from a wearable closet. Fixed: shoes get a wider formality floor (1.0 vs 0.5 — a clean sneaker is valid smart-casual work wear); outerwear is no longer *required* below 15° (that gave anyone without a coat nothing all winter). Empty results now name the blocking slot via `missingCategory()`. **✅ RESOLVED — seasons. Merged (PR #16).** It was the last hard filter in the generator. Plan moved to `done/2026-07-24-seasons-soft-preference.md`. Measured before the fix: on a constructed closet (10 tops / 4 bottoms / 4 shoes, all wearable, the trousers merely lacking a Winter tag) — **40 combos in summer, 0 in winter**, `missingCategory` blaming Bottoms. On the real closet there were **no** dead ends (the old note here claimed winter returned empty; the closet had changed and has 3 winter-tagged bottoms), but winter yielded **21 combos against 60**, and the single coat is tagged `{Spring,Autumn}` so **winter had no outerwear at all**. After: **60/60 in every season**, coat available year-round. Season now ORDERS and SCORES instead of eliminating: `lib/generator/season.ts` (`inSeason`, `seasonFit`, `currentSeason`, case-insensitive because the DB is Title case and fixtures are lower), `eligibleByCategory` puts in-season pieces first so the 200-combo cap keeps the good ones, and `scoreCombo` carries a `SEASON_WEIGHT = 0.2` term. An off-season combo still scores above zero. Two things landed alongside it: - **Material relief** — a weather exclusion may narrow a required slot but may **never empty it**. This also fixed a pre-existing dead end: a closet whose only shoes were suede returned zero outfits in the rain. Relief is scoped to weather; a formality gap is a real gap and is still named. - **Substring material matching** — was equality, so `"suede leather"` already slipped past the rain rule. **⚠️ `HOT_MATERIALS` is a STOPGAP with a planned death date — read before touching warmth.** Deleting the season filter also deleted the only thing keeping a wool sweater out of a July outfit, so `weatherRules` gained material exclusions above 25°C. The user (who knows menswear) corrected the first version, and the correction is the important part: **fibre alone never decides warmth — weight and weave do.** Tropical, fresco and high-twist wools are summer suiting; merino is worn *for* heat because it wicks. `items.material` is a bare fibre name, so a "wool" rule cannot tell a summer-weight trouser from a melton coat, and would bin exactly the smart-casual work wear this app exists to style. So the list is insulation and coarse heavy weave only — `fleece, shearling, down, quilted, puffer, tweed` — where no construction makes them summer-appropriate. Wool/merino/cashmere fall through to the `seasonFit` penalty: demoted, never eliminated. A test pins that a `tropical wool` trouser survives 32°C. The staged plan, because this is **data-blocked, not deferred by choice**: 1. **Now** — the keyword list. It is all free-text `material` can support. 2. **Queue #3 (`item-data-completeness`)** — creates `items.texture` and constrains `material` to an enum. **Do NOT delete the list here**: `fleece`/`down`/`tweed` still match, but `shearling` and `puffer` are absent from the new vocabulary and `quilted` becomes a *texture*, so it silently half-breaks. That plan now carries a "Vocabulary coverage review" section with the fixes (`TEXTURES` needs an `"Other"`; add `Acrylic`, `Shearling`, `Faux leather`, `Modal`). 3. **Queue #12 (`item-signals-in-generator`)** — widen its `textureWarmth(texture)` to `warmth(material, texture)` (texture alone misses tweed, whose warmth is in the cloth), keep a narrow hard exclusion for insulation (a soft term only demotes, and `diversify` fills 20 slots), **then delete `HOT_MATERIALS`.** That plan now carries a "Warmth must read material AND texture" section. Attempting this before #3 makes things worse, not better: `textureWarmth(null)` is `0.5`, so every garment would score identically on warmth. **Limit worth stating even after #12:** `texture` records knit structure, not gsm — a tropical wool and a flannel can both be `Flat`. Nothing in the queue gives weight. ### Deliberate divergence from the design handoff: the occasion row `generator-mockup-v2.html:96` specifies a scrolling chip row with a right-edge gradient fade (`-webkit-mask-image`) and the Refine pill inside the row. We implemented that faithfully — and it was wrong on phones. Measured with the real component: | Shell width | Device | "Evening" visible | |---|---|---| | 375px | iPhone SE / 13 mini | **0%** | | 390px | iPhone 14/15/16 | **0%** | | 414px | Pro Max | 3% | | 440px | shell cap — desktop only | 34% | Refine cost 84px of the row (76px button + 8px gap), so on every real phone **a quarter of the feature was undiscoverable** — the row read "Everyday · Work · Weekend · Refine". The 34% figure is desktop-only and misled the first review; see memory `mobile-first-evaluate-at-phone-width`. **Changed:** `OccasionRow` is now a non-scrolling `flex-1` row of four chips (13px labels), and Refine moved to the header beside "Today's Looks" as `RefineButton`. Refine is a *modifier* on the chosen occasion, not a fifth peer of it, so the header is also the more honest hierarchy. A scroll row suits an unbounded list; four fixed options should all be reachable without a gesture. Verified on an **iPhone 17 simulator** (Xcode is installed but `xcode-select` points at CommandLineTools — use `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer xcrun simctl …`). A test in `occasion-refine.test.tsx` guards the structure (all four chips render; the row has no `overflow-x-auto` or `mask-image`) so this can't silently revert. ## ⚠️ OPEN ITEMS / next steps (in order) 1. **Merge `feat/stylist-generator` → `main`** (PR like the closet work, or direct). # Plans

_Reorganised 2026-07-24._ Three folders, one rule: **a plan moves to `done/` only when its work is
merged to `main`** — not when the plan is written, and not when the branch is green.

| Folder | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `todo/` | Written, **not yet implemented**. Execute in the order below. |
| `done/` | Implemented and merged to `main`. Kept for history — the decisions in them are still the record of *why* the code looks the way it does. |
| `scoping/` | Not TDD plans. Research and scoping documents that need a design decision before a plan can be written. |

> **Read [`REVIEW-2026-07-27.md`](./REVIEW-2026-07-27.md) before executing anything below.** Every plan
> was checked against the current code on 2026-07-27; nine factual defects were fixed *in the plan files*
> (they are already corrected on disk). It also records the open judgment calls, one `wear-stats`
> substitution that needs a second opinion, and what was checked and found fine.

## Execution order (`todo/`)

Two inputs decide this order: `docs/design-review-2026-07-24.md` §8, and **`docs/MONETISATION.md`** §5 —
read that second one before executing anything from #7 onward, because it decides what is gated.

It changed twice on 2026-07-24. First when the full design review showed the "Wear this today" button is
the only wear-log write path in the product (six surfaces read what it writes, so it moved to the front).
Then again when the tiers were defined: **the entitlements seam has to exist before any Pro feature**,
or the gate gets retrofitted into four screens afterwards.

|---|---|---|---|
| ~~1~~ | ~~`2026-07-24-seasons-soft-preference.md`~~ | — | **DONE — merged PR #16**, plan in `done/`. Season now orders + scores instead of filtering; winter went 21 → 60 combos and regained outerwear. Left its `HOT_MATERIALS` stopgap behind — see the note under #3 and #12. |
| ~~2~~ | ~~`2026-07-24-design-tokens.md`~~ | — | **DONE — merged PR #18**, plan in `done/`. Cream `value` step, 7-weight hairline scale, surface gradients; applied to the item card (via the `Surface` primitive), the nav pill and the rust capture FAB. |
| ~~3~~ | ~~`2026-07-24-item-data-completeness.md`~~ | — | **DONE — merged PR #19**, plan in `done/`. One vocabulary module; `material`/`texture` constrained to enums; `items.texture` added; colours/pattern/subcategory/price now editable; legacy materials backfilled. `HOT_MATERIALS` deliberately left alive for #12. |
| **4 ← next** | `2026-07-24-outfit-detail-wear-logging.md` | free | **The unblocker.** Blocks 5, 6, 10. Nothing that reads wears works until this ships. ⚠️ See §2 of `REVIEW-2026-07-27.md`: wearing a look nulls `generated_on`, so it leaves today's set and the stylist screen drops to two looks — decide that deliberately when picking this up. |
| 5 | `2026-07-24-item-detail-rebuild.md` | mixed | Read-first view (free); "Style an outfit with this" is **Pro**. ⚠️ open decision below. Calls the existing `assertCanGenerate` so #7 can widen it underneath. |
| 6 | `2026-07-24-fit-diary.md` | free | Deliberately free — the habit loop is what creates a payer. |
| 7 | **`entitlements`** — *to write* | — | **The seam.** Blocks 8, 10, 11. One place that answers "what may this user do?" |
| 8 | `2026-07-22-regenerate-quota.md` | **Pro** | ⚠️ **Rewrite.** Becomes Pro #1: 3 generations/day free, unlimited on Pro. |
| 9 | `2026-07-24-profile-hub.md` → `2026-07-24-settings.md` | free | The Pro card gets a real state once #7 exists. |

| 12 | `2026-07-24-item-signals-in-generator.md` | — | Texture/pattern in scoring. ## The end-of-build design audit (#16)

**User request, 2026-07-28:** after all `todo/` plans *and* the `scoping/` items are implemented, do a
full design review/audit of the product using **`impeccable`** and **`design-taste-frontend`**.

- **`impeccable` is the primary tool** — it is already configured for this repo (`.impeccable/live/config.json`)
  and reads `DESIGN.md` / `PRODUCT.md`, so it audits against *our* system ("The Midnight Atelier"), not a
  generic one. `/impeccable audit <surface>` per screen, then `polish`.
- **`design-taste-frontend` is a partial fit** — it is written for landing pages, portfolios and
  redesigns. Its audit-first redesign mode applies; its landing-page defaults do not. Fitcheck is a
  mobile-only PWA. Use it as a second opinion on "does this look templated", not as the system of record.
- **Judge at phone width, in the iOS Simulator** — never a resized desktop browser. A desktop-width
  screenshot has already produced false findings on this project once (see the occasion-row measurements
  in `docs/STATE.md`).
- **Sequencing caveat:** `scoping/2026-07-24-womens-wardrobe-scoping.md` adds one-piece garments
  (dresses/jumpsuits), which changes the flat-lay layout templates and the credits list. Auditing the
  visual system *before* that fork lands means auditing it twice. If the women's fork stays deferred
  ("a lot later"), run the audit on the menswear product and re-run the affected screens afterwards.
- Two known items are already parked for this pass: the **10–11px uppercase kickers** (deferred by
  decision 2026-07-24, see below) and the **off-ramp font sizes** the impeccable hook flags in
  `refine-sheet.tsx` / `stylist-view.tsx` / `item-card.tsx`.
- Existing drift is catalogued in `docs/design-review-2026-07-24.md` — read it first so the audit does
  not rediscover what is already written down.

## Open decisions blocking a plan

- **"Style an outfit with this"** (item detail, `Fitcheck.dc.html:654`) conflicts with Decision 5: looks
  are a daily drop, generated once per day, and tapping never calls the model. Styling around a chosen
  item is inherently on-demand. Does it spend an AI call per tap, consume the regenerate quota, or just
  filter the already-stored looks to ones containing that item? This decides whether the button is free
  or is the biggest per-user cost in the product.
- **Wear Stats gap analysis** — *"unlocks 14 new outfits"* is a simulation of what a hypothetical item
  would enable, not a query. Needs designing.
- **"See curated picks"** (`:767`) — a commerce/affiliate surface with no product decision behind it.

1 # Outfit Detail + Wear Logging Implementation Plan 2 3 > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. 4 5 **Goal:** Build the outfit detail screen and the "Wear this today" action — the only wear-log write path in the product, and the thing six other surfaces are waiting on. 6 7 **Architecture:** A new `/outfits/[id]` route renders a stored outfit from `outfits` + `outfit_items`. Two toggles write: `is_favorite` on the outfit row, and a `wear_logs` row keyed `(user_id, outfit_id, worn_on)` so tapping twice cannot double-log. Logging a wear **graduates the outfit out of the daily drop** by nulling `generated_on`, which is what stops a later Regenerate from deleting a look you actually wore. 8 9 **Tech Stack:** Next.js 16 App Router, Server Actions, Supabase (RLS), Vitest, Motion. 10 11 ## Global Constraints 12 13 - **TDD, strictly**: failing test → see it fail → minimal implementation → see it pass → commit. One commit per task. 14 - **Branch → PR → green CI → merge.** `main` is protected. Branch: `feat/outfit-detail-wear-logging`. 15 - **No AI attribution** in commits, PR title or body. 16 - Test: `npx vitest run ` / `npm run test:run`. Types: `npx tsc --noEmit`. Build: `npm run build`. 17 - **RLS on every table, flat policies.** `wear_logs_own` already exists and covers the writes here; no policy changes are needed. 18 - **"Today" is the user's LOCAL date** (`lib/outfits/local-date.ts`), never UTC. A wear logged at 23:00 in Berlin belongs to that day, not the next UTC one. 19 - Server Action modules (`"use server"`) may only export async functions — pure helpers go in `lib/`. 20 21 ## Source 22 23 `design_handoff_stylist_generator/Fitcheck.dc.html:318-365` (outfit detail). Review: 24 `docs/design-review-2026-07-24.md` §6.1. 25 26 ## The two bugs this plan has to fix on the way 27 28 **1. Wearing a look then regenerating currently throws.** `wear_logs.outfit_id references 29 public.outfits(id)` was declared with no `on delete` action, so it is `NO ACTION`. `saveDailyLooks` 30 (`lib/outfits/daily.ts:52`) is delete-then-insert. So: wear a look → tap Regenerate the same day → the 31 delete hits a referenced row → foreign-key violation → regeneration fails. Nobody has hit it because 32 nothing writes `wear_logs` yet. **This plan is what makes it reachable, so it fixes it.** 33 34 The fix is the pin: `generated_on` is nullable and the daily-drop index is 35 `... where generated_on is not null` (`20260722100000_outfits_daily.sql:8-15`). # Plan Review — 2026-07-27

_A read-through of every plan in `todo/` and `scoping/` against the code as it actually is on
`fix/generator-coverage`. Local-only (`docs/` is gitignored)._

**Why this file exists:** the plan files were edited in place during the review, and `docs/` is not in
git — so there is no diff to read afterwards. This records what changed, what was deliberately left
alone, and what was checked and found fine, so none of it has to be rediscovered.

---

## 1. Fixed in the plan files (2026-07-27)

Nine factual defects — things that would have failed on execution, not matters of taste. Already
applied; listed so they are not re-reported.

| Plan | Defect | Fix applied |
|---|---|---|
| `outfit-detail-wear-logging` | Imported `localDateKey`, which **does not exist**. The real export is `localDateFor(now, timeZone)` and it takes a required timezone. 5 call sites. | Corrected name; added the `profiles.location_timezone` read in both `toggleWear` and the page, so an evening wear in Berlin does not log to the next day — the bug the plan's own comment claimed to avoid. |
| `entitlements` | Same `localDateKey` error (2 sites). | Same fix. |
| `entitlements` | `generationsUsedToday` counted **outfit rows**. `saveDailyLooks` writes one row per *look* (3 per generation), so a free user was blocked after 1 generation, not 3. | Counts **distinct occasions** for the day. Takes `(userId, today)`; `assertCanGenerate` passes the local date the action already computed, rather than re-deriving it from the server clock. |
| `entitlements` | Task 2's test imported the `server-only` module and could not resolve under jsdom — the plan admitted this two steps later without fixing the import. | Pure functions (`entitlementsFor`, `checkGenerations`) moved into `tiers.ts`; `entitlements.ts` re-exports them; the test imports `../tiers`. |
| `seasons-soft-preference` | Task 4 Step 7 said *"replace everything from `isEligible` through the end of `buildCandidates`"* and pasted a **pre-fix** body — top-major nested loop, `slice(0, CAP)`, `outer[0]`, `accessories[0]`. Executing it reverts the coverage fix (tops 20→1, coats 3→1, accessories 3→1). | The pasted loop is gone, replaced by an explicit do-not-rewrite warning and a 4-step surgical edit list. Stale line refs and the stale `outer[0]` comment corrected. `coverage.test.ts` named in Global Constraints as the regression guard. |
| `item-signals-in-generator` | The "mild weather" test asserted the chunky/fine gap is `< 0.2`; the implementation in the same task yields **0.59** (at 18°, `want = 0.28` → 0.38 vs 0.97). The task could never go green. | Replaced with a relative assertion — the mild gap is narrower than the cold gap (0.59 < 0.65). The inaccurate `want`-sits-near-0.5 comment corrected too. |
| `route-url-audit` | Task 3 creates `app/outfits/[outfitId]/`, but `outfit-detail-wear-logging` (queue #4) already builds `app/outfits/[id]/`. content.content:
-- The daily drop (see CLAUDE.md "Decision 5"): looks are generated ONCE per
-- local day per occasion and then read back, not regenerated on every tap.
--
-- generated_on is the USER'S local date (lib/outfits/local-date.ts), never UTC.
-- look_index is the position within the day's set of three, so the order the
-- stylist chose survives a round trip.
alter table public.outfits
  add column if not exists generated_on date,
  add column if not exists look_index    smallint;

-- One row per (user, occasion, day, position). A regenerate deletes the day's
-- rows and re-inserts, so this also stops a double-submit writing six looks.
create unique index if not exists outfits_daily_unique
  on public.outfits (user_id, occasion, generated_on, look_index)
  where generated_on is not null;

-- The read path: "today's set for this occasion".
create index if not exists outfits_daily_lookup
  on public.outfits (user_id, occasion, generated_on);
=== wear_logs ===
-- Plan 06 (Stylist generator): outfits / outfit_items / wear_logs + flat RLS.
-- outfits also persist the chosen look_name + per-look garment layout so a saved
-- outfit re-renders identically (README §8).

create table public.outfits (
  id               uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id          uuid not null references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
  name             text,
  look_name        text,
  occasion         text,
  weather_snapshot jsonb,
  layout           jsonb,
  ai_reasoning     text,
  is_favorite      boolean default false,
  created_at       timestamptz default now()
);

create table public.outfit_items (
  outfit_id uuid not null references public.outfits(id) on delete cascade,
  item_id   uuid not null references public.items(id)   on delete cascade,
  slot      text not null,
  primary key (outfit_id, item_id)
);

create table public.wear_logs (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    uuid not null references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
  outfit_id  uuid references public.outfits(id),
  worn_on    date not null,
  occasion   text,
  photo_url  text,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

alter table public.outfits      enable row level security;
alter table public.outfit_items enable row level security;
alter table public.wear_logs    enable row level security;

create policy outfits_own on public.outfits
  for all using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id) with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
create policy wear_logs_own on public.wear_logs
  for all using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id) with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
create policy outfit_items_own on public.outfit_items
  for all
  using (exists (select 1 from public.outfits o where o.id = outfit_id and o.user_id = (select auth.uid())))
  with check (exists (select 1 from public.outfits o where o.id = outfit_id and o.user_id = (select auth.uid())));

-- Chosen-city label for the weather strip (D8; geolocation shows "Current location").
alter table public.profiles add column if not exists location_label text;

Base directory for this skill: /Users/1curafu/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.2.0/skills/executing-plans

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

**Note:** Tell your human partner that Superpowers works much better with access to subagents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Codex App, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all qualify; see the per-platform tool refs in `../using-superpowers/references/`). If subagents are available, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development instead of this skill.

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Ensure an isolated workspace: use superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one
2. Read plan file
3. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
4. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
5. If no concerns: Create todos for the plan items and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember

-- One wear per outfit per day. The "Wear this today" button is a TOGGLE, and a
-- double tap (or a retried Server Action) must not produce two rows — every
-- wear count in the product is a count of these.
create unique index if not exists wear_logs_unique_day
  on public.wear_logs (user_id, outfit_id, worn_on)
  where outfit_id is not null;

-- Reading a wear back needs the outfit; reading the diary needs the date.
create index if not exists wear_logs_user_day_idx
  on public.wear_logs (user_id, worn_on desc);

-- The FK was declared with no ON DELETE action (NO ACTION), so deleting an
-- outfit that had been worn raised a foreign-key violation. saveDailyLooks is
-- delete-then-insert, so a Regenerate after a wear would have failed outright.
--
-- The primary fix lives in lib/outfits/daily.ts: a worn outfit is PINNED — it is
-- excluded from the day's delete, so it survives a Regenerate and stays in the
-- day's set. This constraint is the second line of defence, so any future delete
-- path degrades to "wear kept, outfit forgotten" instead of a 500.
alter table public.wear_logs
  drop constraint if exists wear_logs_outfit_id_fkey;
alter table public.wear_logs
  add constraint wear_logs_outfit_id_fkey
  foreign key (outfit_id) references public.outfits(id) on delete set null;

**The CTA — you're right.** The design has an explicit "See the full look" (`Fitcheck.dc.html:312`); I'd wrapped the flat-lay in an invisible link, which nobody would find. Fixing that.

**The credits line — I'd keep it.** It's already clickable: each name opens that item (`stylist.tsx:236` → `/closet/[id]`). So deleting it *removes* the item path from the stylist screen rather than adding one. It's also the only thing naming what those silhouettes are before you tap through — and the design keeps a piece list on that screen too ("THE 4 PIECES"), just as thumbnails instead of a credit line. What's genuinely missing is the opposite: the **detail** screen's "In this look" rows aren't clickable. Adding that.

132:## 3. Typography
133-
134-**Display Font:** Libre Caslon Text (serif fallback) — 400, 700, and 400 italic, loaded via `next/font/google` as `--font-serif`
135-**Body Font:** Hanken Grotesk (system-ui fallback) — 300–700, loaded as `--font-sans`
136-
137-**Character:** A classic high-contrast serif against a warm, quiet grotesk — the pairing of a fashion magazine masthead and its picture captions. The serif carries identity and voice; the sans disappears into function.
138-
139-### Hierarchy
140-- **Display** (Caslon 400, ~4.5rem, 0.92 line-height, −0.02em): The wordmark and welcome-screen moments only.
141-- **Headline** (Caslon 400, 1.875rem, 1.12 line-height, −0.01em): Screen titles — "The Closet", "Today's Looks".
142-- **Reasoning** (Caslon 400 *italic*, ~1.0625rem): The stylist's "why it works" line and taglines, led by a Terracotta Rust `J` glyph. This is the product's voice — it is never truncated, never shrunk to caption size.
143-- **Body** (Hanken 400, 1rem, 1.5): All functional copy. Cap prose at 65–75ch.
144-- **Label / Kicker** (Hanken 500, 11px, +0.22em, UPPERCASE, Warm Gray Dim): Micro-labels like "19 PIECES". The brand kicker variant on the welcome screen runs 13px, +0.34em, in rust.
145-
146-### Named Rules
147-**The Italic Why Rule.** AI stylist reasoning is always serif italic with the rust `J` glyph — hero treatment, not a caption. Any new surface that shows an outfit inherits this treatment unchanged.
148-
149-**The Two-Voices Rule.** Serif speaks (identity, titles, reasoning); sans works (buttons, forms, data). Never set UI controls in the serif; never set a screen title in the sans.
150-
151-## 4. Elevation
152-
153-The system is flat and tonal. Depth is conveyed by the surface ramp (Canvas → Surface 1 → 2 → 3) plus a 1px inset cream hairline (`inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(237,230,216,0.07)`) on cards — the look of layered dark paper, not floating glass. There are no drop shadows anywhere. The bottom navigation uses a `backdrop-blur` over 90%-opacity canvas, the one sanctioned translucency in the system. The global film-grain overlay (fractal-noise SVG at 5% opacity, `mix-blend-overlay`) sits above all surfaces at the top of the z-scale.
154-
155-### Named Rules
156-**The Hairline Rule.** Cards and inputs are bounded by cream at 7–12% opacity, never by shadow. If a surface needs more separation, step up the tonal ramp instead of adding a shadow.
157-

content.text: Good catch — and no, it shouldn't be 4. "Today's Looks" is a set of three and the index tabs are literally 01/02/03; a fourth tab doesn't fit at 390px. Let me check how the count is requested:

input.command: grep -n "count\|slice\|3\b" lib/generator/rerank.ts | head -20
input.description: Find how many picks rerank returns

content.content:
44	// `z.toJSONSchema` cannot represent a transform ("Transforms cannot be
45	// represented in JSON Schema"); the repair belongs on the way in, not the way out.
46	const PickShape = z.object({
47	  combo_index: z.number().int(),
48	  name: z.string().min(1),
49	  why: z.string().min(1),
50	});
51	
52	// Sanitised JSON Schema for Anthropic's output_config.format (strips min/max keywords
53	// that would 400 — real bounds re-enforced by RerankSchema.parse after the call).
54	export const rerankJsonSchema = forStructuredOutput(
55	  z.toJSONSchema(z.object({ picks: z.array(PickShape).length(3) })),
56	) as Record<string, unknown>;
57	
58	/** The most looks a daily drop ever shows. */
59	export const MAX_PICKS = 3;
60	
61	// The PARSE shape — same fields, plus the name repair.
62	//
63	// `.min(1)`, NOT `.length(3)`. The count is never enforced ON the model —
64	// `forStructuredOutput` strips minItems/maxItems because the API 400s on them —
65	// so an exact-3 rule existed only as a post-hoc throw, and a closet with fewer
66	// than three viable combos failed the ENTIRE generation as "Couldn't reach the
67	// stylist". That is a lie: the stylist answered, with everything the wardrobe
68	// could give. It bites hardest right after onboarding's "capture your first
69	// five", which is the magic moment. Repair, don't reject — the same stance as

input.command:
gh pr create --title "feat: outfit detail and wear logging" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Builds the outfit detail screen and the "Wear this today" action — the only
wear-log write path in the product. Times worn, cost-per-wear, last worn, the
Fit Diary grid, streaks, most-worn and gathering-dust are all views over what
this button writes, and nothing wrote to `wear_logs` before now.

## The latent bug this makes reachable, and fixes

`wear_logs.outfit_id` had no `ON DELETE` action, and `saveDailyLooks` is
delete-then-insert — so wearing a look and then regenerating the same day raised
a foreign-key violation and the regeneration failed outright.

A worn outfit is now **pinned**: `saveDailyLooks` excludes anything with a wear
log from the day's delete, and numbers the fresh set past it. The FK also
degrades to `ON DELETE SET NULL` as a second line of defence.

The plan's original fix was to null `generated_on` so the worn outfit left the
daily drop. That works, but the user-visible consequence is that tapping "Wear
this today" makes the look vanish from the stylist screen with no explanation.
Pinning keeps it visible and badged, and un-wearing just clears the badge.

A pinned look still **counts toward the day's three** — the re-ranker is asked
for `3 − pinned` fresh looks rather than a full set, so the day's set never grows
a fourth. The index tabs are 01/02/03 and a fourth does not fit at 390px.

A unique index on `(user_id, outfit_id, worn_on)` makes the toggle idempotent, so
a double tap or a retried action cannot inflate a wear count.

Also threads the outfit id through `loadDailyLooks`, which never selected it — so
until now a look on the stylist screen had nowhere to go.

## Stylist screen

- **"See the full look"** is the way into a look. Wrapping the flat-lay in an
  unlabelled link was tried first and is not discoverable — the flat-lay reads as
  a picture, not a control.
- **The credit line is gone.** The detail screen now lists every piece with its
  brand, image and category, and each row opens the same garment page — so the
  line was a second copy of that list costing ~200px of the fold.
- **Regenerate** was a bare uppercase line that read as a caption; an icon-only
  button beside the primary was tried and rejected (nothing tells you a ⟳ means
  "spend an AI call"). It is now a bounded secondary control with its words.
- The rust `f` glyph sat ~3px low: `align-middle` centres on x-height, and it
  carried a further downward nudge on top.

## Verified

Full suite green (324), tsc clean, build clean. Live on an iPhone 17 Pro
simulator and in the browser against the local stack: wear, unwear, double-tap
(exactly one row in the database, no duplicates), and a Regenerate after a wear —
the case that used to fail — which succeeded and produced a three-look set with
the worn look pinned at index 0.
EOF

content.text:
CI green. **[PR #20](https://github.com/1curafu/Fitcheck/pull/20)** is up — queue #4, the wear-logging unblocker.

**What shipped**

- `/outfits/[id]` — the detail screen: stored flat-lay geometry, the italic why, and every piece linking to its garment page.
- "Wear this today" — the product's first `wear_logs` write, keyed on the user's *local* date. Six planned surfaces read what this writes.
- Fixed a latent crash: `wear_logs.outfit_id` had no `ON DELETE` action and `saveDailyLooks` is delete-then-insert, so wear → Regenerate on the same day was a foreign-key violation. Nobody had hit it because nothing wrote wear logs yet — this feature is what made it reachable.

**Where I diverged from the plan, and why**

The plan fixed that crash by nulling `generated_on` so a worn look left the daily drop. You chose to keep it visible instead, so a worn outfit is now *pinned*: excluded from the day's delete, badged `WORN TODAY`, and un-wearing just clears the badge. Your catch on the 4th look was right — a pinned look now counts toward the day's three, so the re-ranker is asked for `3 − pinned` rather than a full set.

Also on your calls: the credit line is gone (the detail screen carries that list, and each row opens the garment), "See the full look" replaced the invisible flat-lay link, Regenerate got a real button shell with its words, and the rust `f` was sitting ~3px low.

**Verified live**, not just green: wear → unwear → wear left exactly one row with no duplicates, and Regenerate-after-wear succeeded, producing a three-look set with the worn one pinned at index 0.

Two things to flag: the local DB now has a real wear log and a regenerated work set for today (two Haiku calls spent on the verification), and the merge is yours to make — I haven't merged it.

The top gap is the same class of bug, one level up: the layout sets `viewportFit: "cover"` + a translucent status bar, so in the **installed PWA** content runs *under* the status bar — but no screen accounts for `env(safe-area-inset-top)`. Instead each one hard-codes its own guess (`pt-[46px]` on the stylist, `py-8` on the closet, nothing on the diary). In Safari, where the viewport already starts below the status bar, those constants land on top of it — that's the doubled gap you're seeing.

The fix is the shell owning the top inset once, with screens keeping only their design padding. But that touches every screen and needs a look at each:

## IN FLIGHT — PR #20, branch `feat/outfit-detail-wear-logging`

Queue #4 (`outfit-detail-wear-logging`). CI green, live-verified, **awaiting the user's merge.**

**The plan's `generated_on = null` approach was REJECTED by the user.** The plan fixed the FK
violation by nulling `generated_on` so a worn look left the daily drop; the user chose to keep it
visible. So a worn outfit is **pinned**: `saveDailyLooks` excludes anything with a wear log from the
day's delete and numbers the fresh set past it (`freshIndexStart` in `lib/outfits/wear.ts`).
`toggleWear` never touches the outfit row. Un-wearing just clears the badge.

**A pinned look COUNTS toward the day's three** — `rerank` gained a `want` arg and the action passes
`MAX_PICKS - pinned.length`. Without it the set grew a fourth look on every wear-then-regenerate, and
the index tabs are 01/02/03 (a fourth does not fit at 390px). The user caught this.

**Design decisions made live with the user on this branch (all theirs):**
- **The `Credits` component is DELETED**, not just unmounted — the stylist screen's magazine credit
  line duplicated the detail screen's piece list and cost ~200px of the fold. Its D2 test ("brand
  names are the most readable") went with it; `why-credits.test.tsx` is now `why-quote.test.tsx`.
  `onOpenItem` was removed from `StylistView`/`Stylist` — the detail rows carry the item links now.
- **"See the full look"** is the way into a look. Wrapping the flat-lay in an unlabelled link was
  tried first and rejected as undiscoverable.
- **Regenerate**: bare uppercase line → icon-only button beside the primary (**rejected — nothing
  tells you ⟳ means "spend an AI call"**) → bounded secondary control with icon AND words.
- The rust `f` glyph in `WhyQuote` sat ~3px low (`align-middle` centres on x-height, plus a stray
  downward nudge).

**⚠️ `MobileShell`'s `overflow-hidden` was the reason the bottom nav only appeared at the end of the
page.** `overflow: hidden` makes an element a scroll container, so a `position: sticky` descendant
sticks to THAT box, not the viewport. Now `overflow-x-clip` — same 440px clipping, no scroll
container. A test in `mobile-nav.test.tsx` guards it. `/generate`'s `pb-[76px]` was removed (the nav
is 107px and reserves its own space in flow).

**NEXT, agreed with the user (2026-07-30): the top safe-area inset, as its own branch after #20
merges.** Same class of bug as the nav. `app/layout.tsx` sets `viewportFit: "cover"` +
`black-translucent`, so in the installed PWA content runs UNDER the status bar — but nothing reads
`env(safe-area-inset-top)`. Every screen hard-codes a different guess instead: `pt-[46px]`
(`stylist-view.tsx`), `py-8` (closet), nothing (diary/profile), `top-[58px]` (the detail back button).
In Safari those constants stack on top of a viewport that already clears the status bar — hence the
large empty band at the top. Fix: the **shell** owns the top inset once
(`pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]`), screens keep only their design padding. Touches every screen, so
screenshot each at phone width. `MobileNav` already got the bottom half of this
(`pb-[max(26px,env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]`) — that gap is home-indicator clearance, not slack.

**Local DB was modified by the verification:** one `wear_logs` row for `2026-07-30`, and today's
`work` set was regenerated twice (two real Haiku calls).

viewport already clears the status bar, those constants stacked on top of it —
that empty band at the top of every screen.

flat `pb-[30px]` — which measured as 26px and 30px of dead space in a browser.

tab, clear of the home indicator in standalone.

  falls out to the stylist screen. Covered by tests in both directions.

  selecting look 03 and coming back returned you to 01, and a manual switch to

simulator: measured 28px to first content (was 46px + the status bar) and 12px

content.text:
**[PR #21](https://github.com/1curafu/Fitcheck/pull/21) is green** — yours to merge. Also did the housekeeping from #20 (branch deleted, plan moved to `done/`, queue #5 marked next).

**The safe-area fix.** One `.screen-top` utility in `globals.css` now carries `env(safe-area-inset-top)`, replacing the hard-coded status-bar allowance every screen had invented for itself. Measured before/after: **46px + the status bar → 28px** to first content, and **26px → 12px** under the nav pill. The bottom insets were the same mistake as `max(26px, …)` — floored instead of additive, so they never collapsed to zero in a browser where the toolbar already occupies that band.

**Three bugs turned up while verifying, all real:**

- **Back was dead on the outfit detail** when you land there directly — a shared link, a refresh, or a PWA cold start. `router.back()` with no history silently does nothing. That's exactly why it looked broken to you: I'd been opening detail URLs directly in the simulator. Now falls out to `/generate`, tested both ways.
- **The stylist screen lost your place** — you were right, and it was worse than just the look: a manual switch to Weekend also reverted to the predicted occasion. Both now live in the URL. Two traps in getting there: `useSearchParams()` doesn't observe `history.replaceState`, so my first attempt silently no-opped; and the geolocation refresh re-runs `generate`, so a consume-once restore got wiped by the second result.
- The detail stage had a hand-rolled copy of the `.surface-stage` gradient — now the design-system class.

On the gradient: it *is* rendering, it's just ~18 RGB levels by design. You chose to keep the handoff's values, so `.surface-stage` is unchanged — noted in `STATE.md` so it doesn't get re-litigated.

One caveat worth stating: the landing page and onboarding quiz got the same `.screen-top` change but I couldn't screenshot them — both are behind auth state you've already passed. The change is mechanical and the build is clean, but they're unverified visually.

1	# Plan Review — 2026-07-27
2	
3	_A read-through of every plan in `todo/` and `scoping/` against the code as it actually is on
4	`fix/generator-coverage`. Local-only (`docs/` is gitignored)._
5	
6	**Why this file exists:** the plan files were edited in place during the review, and `docs/` is not in
7	git — so there is no diff to read afterwards. This records what changed, what was deliberately left
8	alone, and what was checked and found fine, so none of it has to be rediscovered.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Fixed in the plan files (2026-07-27)
13	
14	Nine factual defects — things that would have failed on execution, not matters of taste. Already
15	applied; listed so they are not re-reported.
16	
17	| Plan | Defect | Fix applied |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| `outfit-detail-wear-logging` | Imported `localDateKey`, which **does not exist**. The real export is `localDateFor(now, timeZone)` and it takes a required timezone. 5 call sites. | Corrected name; added the `profiles.location_timezone` read in both `toggleWear` and the page, so an evening wear in Berlin does not log to the next day — the bug the plan's own comment claimed to avoid. |
20	| `entitlements` | Same `localDateKey` error (2 sites). | Same fix. |
21	| `entitlements` | `generationsUsedToday` counted **outfit rows**. `saveDailyLooks` writes one row per *look* (3 per generation), so a free user was blocked after 1 generation, not 3. | Counts **distinct occasions** for the day. Takes `(userId, today)`; `assertCanGenerate` passes the local date the action already computed, rather than re-deriving it from the server clock. |
22	| `entitlements` | Task 2's test imported the `server-only` module and could not resolve under jsdom — the plan admitted this two steps later without fixing the import. | Pure functions (`entitlementsFor`, `checkGenerations`) moved into `tiers.ts`; `entitlements.ts` re-exports them; the test imports `../tiers`. |
23	| `seasons-soft-preference` | Task 4 Step 7 said *"replace everything from `isEligible` through the end of `buildCandidates`"* and pasted a **pre-fix** body — top-major nested loop, `slice(0, CAP)`, `outer[0]`, `accessories[0]`. Executing it reverts the coverage fix (tops 20→1, coats 3→1, accessories 3→1). | The pasted loop is gone, replaced by an explicit do-not-rewrite warning and a 4-step surgical edit list. Stale line refs and the stale `outer[0]` comment corrected. `coverage.test.ts` named in Global Constraints as the regression guard. |
24	| `item-signals-in-generator` | The "mild weather" test asserted the chunky/fine gap is `< 0.2`; the implementation in the same task yields **0.59** (at 18°, `want = 0.28` → 0.38 vs 0.97). The task could never go green. | Replaced with a relative assertion — the mild gap is narrower than the cold gap (0.59 < 0.65). The inaccurate `want`-sits-near-0.5 comment corrected too. |
25	| `route-url-audit` | Task 3 creates `app/outfits/[outfitId]/`, but `outfit-detail-wear-logging` (queue #4) already builds `app/outfits/[id]/`. Two slug names on one dynamic segment is a **Next.js build error**. | Task 3 marked superseded, collapsed into a `<details>` block, replaced by a verify-only step. File table and Task 5 text updated to `[id]`. |
26	| `route-url-audit` | Task 5 ends `git add CLAUDE.md docs/STATE.md` — both gitignored (`.gitignore:36`, `.gitignore:34`), so the commit fails on an empty index and the task blocks. | Replaced with "edit both, nothing to commit here". |
27	| `wear-stats` | `countCombos` summed `buildCandidates(...).length`, which stops at `CAP = 200` — so any sizeable closet returns 200 before *and* after the hypothetical piece, every `unlocks` is 0, and the gap card never renders for the users who would pay for it. | Counts the product of eligible required slots instead. **See §3 — the replacement formula is a judgment call, not a mechanical fix.** |
28	| `wear-stats` | `expect(gap === null \|\| gap.unlocks > 0).toBe(true)` is a tautology given the implementation only sets `best` when `unlocks > 0`. Cannot fail. | Asserts the real contract: any returned gap has a positive count and names a real candidate. |
29	| `regenerate-quota`, `cutout-backfill` | Dependency paths pointed at `plans/2026-07-22-*.md`; both files are now in `plans/done/`. | Repointed. |
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Deliberately NOT changed — decided, not defects
34	
35	Raised during the review and left alone: these are product decisions already made, or matters of taste.
36	Recorded so a future review does not re-open them as findings.
37	
38	- **Wearing a look nulls `generated_on`, so it leaves today's set.** Correct fix for the FK problem, and
39	  intentional per the plan. The user-visible consequence — tap "Wear this today" and the stylist screen
40	  drops to two looks — is not written down anywhere, and nothing checks how `loadDailyLooks` /
41	  `reassembleLooks` behave with a partial set. Worth a deliberate answer when
42	  `outfit-detail-wear-logging` is picked up, not a plan edit now.
43	- **Profile hub's "outfits" stat counts every `outfits` row ever** (~12/day at 3 looks × 4 occasions),
44	  with no filter. Probably wants distinct days or favourites. Design call.
45	- **`updatePreferences` is read-modify-write**, while its comment claims it stops two open screens
46	  reverting each other. It doesn't — a SQL-side `preferences || $patch::jsonb` would. Near-impossible
47	  race for a single user; comment accuracy only.
48	- **`/generate` → `/today` sweep.** `README.md:37` settles the ordering (route-audit runs last), so the
49	  later plans hard-coding `/generate` are correct when they run. But route-audit has **no sweep task**
50	  for the four references they introduce: `settings.md` and `outfit-detail-wear-logging.md`
51	  (`revalidatePath("/generate")`), `fit-diary.md` (empty-state link), and `design-tokens.md`, whose nav
52	  test asserts the label `"Stylist"` that route-audit renames to `"Today"`. Add a sweep step when
53	  route-audit is picked up.
54	- **`regenerate-quota` has no rewrite banner in the file.** `README.md:31` and `MONETISATION.md:162`
55	  both mark it ⚠️ rewrite → Pro #1, but a worker opening only the plan file implements the superseded
56	  `profiles.plan` design.
57	- **`wear-stats` has no Pro gate.** `README.md:33` already flags this; the plan still has none.
58	- **README/plan drift:** `README.md:43-47` lists *"Style an outfit with this"* as an open decision
59	  blocking a plan, but `item-detail-rebuild.md:22-36` has already decided it (filter today's stored
60	  looks; fall back to a quota-consuming generation). One of the two should move.
61	- **`GAP_CANDIDATES` is menswear-only** (oxford, loafers, wool trousers). Consistent with the women's
62	  wardrobe being deferred (`README.md:56`) — flagged only so it is revisited with that work.
63	
64	---
65	
66	## 3. One substitution that needs your eye
67	
68	`wear-stats` Task 2's `countCombos` was rewritten from "count what `buildCandidates` returns" to
69	"multiply the eligible required-slot counts". The **bug** was real and mechanical (the `CAP` makes the
70	old version return 0 for real closets). The **replacement** is a modelling choice:
71	
72	- It counts *buildable* outfits, ignoring the cap — which is what *"unlocks 14 new outfits"* claims.
73	- It ignores outerwear and accessories entirely (`maxAccessories: 0` was already the plan's intent).
74	- It grows multiplicatively, so numbers get large fast on a real closet. `Grey wool trousers` in a
75	  20-top / 20-shoe closet reads as "+400 outfits", which is true and probably not what you want to
76	  print. A presentation cap, or counting only the *marginal* pieces, may be the better claim.
77	
78	It also now depends on `eligibleByCategory`, which `seasons-soft-preference` creates — that dependency
79	has been added to the plan's constraints.
80	
81	`README.md:48` already lists the gap analysis as an open decision. This is the specific technical reason
82	it needs one.
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 4. Checked and found fine — do not re-raise
87	
88	- **`entitlements` adds `outfits_user_generated_idx (user_id, generated_on)`.** Not redundant with
89	  `outfits_daily_lookup`, which is `(user_id, occasion, generated_on)` — `occasion` is the second
90	  column, so it cannot serve the meter's predicate.
91	- **`wear_logs` FK surgery** in `outfit-detail-wear-logging` Task 1 is sound. `outfit_id` is nullable
92	  (`20260718090000_outfits.sql:28`), so `on delete set null` is valid, and the inline unnamed constraint
93	  auto-names to `wear_logs_outfit_id_fkey`, so the `drop constraint if exists` matches.
94	- **`Fitcheck.dc.html` authority.** `README.md:72-76` already corrects the old "byte-identical duplicate,
95	  ignore it" claim. `docs/STATE.md:114` still carries the stale version, and
96	  `item-data-completeness.md:1087` already schedules that fix.
97	- **`score.ts` being rewritten by two plans.** `item-signals-in-generator.md:224` explicitly says to keep
98	  the season term, and README orders seasons #1 / item-signals #12. Anticipated, not a conflict.
99	- **`fit-diary` date arithmetic.** Spot-checked: 1 July 2026 is a Wednesday (2 lead cells), 2028 is a
100	  leap year, the streak cases and the 204-day gathering-dust figure all compute correctly.
101	- **All docs cited by the plans exist**: `MONETISATION.md`, `design-review-2026-07-24.md`, `BUGS.md`,
102	  `prototype-review.md`, `Fitcheck.dc.html`.
103	
104	---
105	
106	## 5. A question the plans cannot answer themselves
107	
108	`MONETISATION.md:25-29` says the daily drop **must never be gated**. `MONETISATION.md:37,76` puts the
109	drop inside the 3/day meter ("drop + regenerates + other occasions"). With four occasions each needing
110	its own generation, a free user who taps all four is blocked on the fourth — having only ever used the
111	product as intended, never once tapping Regenerate.
112	
113	Not a bug in any plan; both readings are written down as policy. Worth resolving before `entitlements`
114	(queue #7) ships, since it is the plan that makes the choice real.
115

118	## 6. Scoping docs
119	
120	All three are in good shape and correctly refuse to be plans. Two cross-links worth adding when they are

122	
123	- **Packing mode's capsule solve and wear-stats' gap analysis are the same computation** ("which item
